title: Accept only verified merged child archives in stacked PR validation
outOfScope: Accepting an archive by task name, local worktree path, or mutable Closure Receipt.
Changing release state, installation content, or unrelated Work Item lifecycle behavior.

sources.reason: The aggregate PR validator currently accepts only the receipt-bound historical prefix or source-linked recoveries, so it rejects valid later child PR archives merged into the active parent branch.
Regression coverage establishes the existing one-new-Work-Item and historical-receipt fail-closed boundaries.
The immutable receipt binds only archive sequences 674–676 and exposes why later merged children cannot be inferred through the adjacent-source rule.
A real later child Contract with a valid Start Receipt must be accepted only when its archive pair is proven to have entered parent ancestry through a merge commit.
The authoritative lifecycle reference already documents exceptional stacked closure and historical recovery boundaries that this validator must preserve.

riskAssessment.reason: An overly broad exception could let arbitrary unrelated archive pairs bypass the one-Work-Item PR boundary; acceptance must bind a valid Start Receipt, immutable Contract/Summary pair, and a two-parent merge in the parent branch ancestry.

executionDecision.reason: The user explicitly directed process-defect correction before release and permitted focused verification without a full test run for this repair.

preReviewWarnings: Review the proof that each accepted child archive entered the parent ancestry through a two-parent merge, rather than merely being reachable from HEAD.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: A PR may exempt an archived child Work Item from the one-new-Work-Item count only when its Contract/Summary pair, Start Receipt binding, archive-addition commit, and a later two-parent merge into the checked parent ancestry are all verified.
The actual #473 archive chain passes aggregate PR validation without changing any immutable archived Contract, Summary, or historical recovery receipt.
An archive with a missing or invalid Start Receipt, no archive-addition commit, no qualifying merge, or a direct/non-merged addition remains rejected and cannot suppress the one-new-Work-Item error.
The existing exact historical-receipt and source-linked recovery paths remain fail closed, and English/Japanese lifecycle references describe the additional verified-merged-child boundary.
guidelines: Preserve one Work Item, one branch, and one PR as the default; accept stacked child evidence only after deterministic Git and receipt proof.
Do not use task-name allowlists, mutable local Closure Receipts, or a broad reachability-only exception.
Use focused regression and validator commands under the user's temporary no-full-test authorization.

intent.problem: PR #473 contains WI-10 and later corrective child Work Items that were separately merged into its active parent branch. The aggregate PR validator validates a historical receipt only through archive sequence 676, then rejects the later children because their immutable Contracts cannot retroactively cite a predecessor source. This blocks the parent PR despite valid child PR merges and Start Receipts.
constraints: Keep direct PR validation and the normal one-Work-Item-per-PR boundary fail closed.
Do not rewrite archived evidence or extend the historical receipt by hand.
Require valid Start Receipt binding, paired archive provenance, and a qualifying two-parent parent-branch merge for every exception.
Run focused tests and checks only; do not run full quality or full pytest under the user's temporary instruction.
intent.rationale: The repair must model the actual nested-PR lifecycle in verifiable repository history, so future corrective children neither block their parent PR nor create an unreviewed archive bypass.

declaredIntent.summary: Repair stacked parent-PR archive validation using deterministic repository evidence while preserving direct-PR and archive-integrity fail-closed boundaries.
